result.title: RoAR-VAE: Improving Latent Diffusability through Robust Prediction
result.summary: An effective visual tokenizer must preserve image fidelity while producing latents that downstream diffusion models can learn efficiently. Prior work improves latent diffusability through semantic alignment or joint tokenizer--diffusion training. Revisiting REPA-E, a representative approach, we find that removing its diffusion objective and dedicated generative blocks while retaining semantic prediction from corrupted latents yields comparable downstream generation performance under a matched setting. This observation motivates a general principle of robust prediction: generation-relevant information should remain recoverable from corrupted latents. We instantiate this principle with two complementary objectives. RobustAlign predicts pretrained semantic features from corrupted latents to preserve high-level structure, while RobustRecon reconstructs the clean image to retain fine-grained spatial and appearance information. Together, they form Robust Alignment and Reconstruction VAE (RoAR-VAE). Our analysis suggests that robust prediction improves diffusability by making useful information more accessible in high-variance latent directions, which diffusion models tend to learn earlier. Empirically, RoAR-VAE improves average generation benchmark performance by 2.19 points over the strongest baseline tokenizer under the same training budget, while improving small-text reconstruction accuracy by 16.93 percentage points over FLUX.1-VAE. These results demonstrate that RoAR-VAE achieves a favorable balance between reconstruction fidelity and downstream generative learnability.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RoAR-VAE：在视觉 tokenizer 训练中，从被破坏的 latent 出发分别预测预训练语义特征（RobustAlign）并重建干净图像（RobustRecon），以提升 latent 的可扩散性，并在生成基准与文本重建精度上报告改进。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「生成相关信息应可从被破坏 latent 中恢复」的鲁棒预测目标，可能为 LVR 中保持 latent 内部状态的视觉细节、缓解信息坍缩的辅助监督提供可核查线索，但研究对象是图像生成 tokenizer 而非多模态推理。
